claims.text: The component alloy is susceptible to hot cracking during fusion welding.
Segregation of low-melting phases along grain boundaries can cause the stated hot-cracking susceptibility.
A FeCrNiTiZr-like high-entropy-alloy overlay is suitable for laser-cladding repair of the component.
Laser cladding can be performed with sufficiently low heat input to avoid full substrate fusion.
Laser cladding will produce a refined, predominantly single-phase overlay microstructure.
Laser cladding will minimize segregation and the formation of low-melting-point interdendritic phases in the overlay.
The refined and less-segregated overlay microstructure will reduce stress concentrations and hot-crack nucleation sites.
Avoiding full melting and rapid solidification will limit liquation cracking and hot cracking.
The tailored high-entropy-alloy overlay has improved fracture toughness and wear resistance.
The high-entropy-alloy overlay will bond metallurgically to the substrate.
The overlay will provide a protective, crack-resistant layer.
The laser-clad repair will have significantly less hot cracking than a traditional fusion-welded repair.
The laser-clad repair will have better adhesion than a traditional fusion-welded repair.
The laser-clad repair will have better fatigue performance under aggressive service conditions than a traditional fusion-welded repair.
The laser-clad repair will have better wear performance under aggressive service conditions than a traditional fusion-welded repair.
Traditional fusion-welding repair is ineffective because a wide solidification range and segregation of low-melting components produce hot cracks.
The proposed approach is limited when damage is extremely severe or when laser access is restricted.

contradictions.description: The mechanism broadly describes laser cladding as avoiding full melting and rapid solidification, although laser cladding normally melts and rapidly solidifies the deposited material and commonly a shallow substrate region to establish the claimed metallurgical bond. The conditions more narrowly state that full substrate fusion is avoided, so the distinction between avoiding bulk substrate melting and avoiding melting altogether is internally unclear.
